posture: A quiet NSW day in week two of the new regime: no fresh SIRA, icare, Personal Injury Commission or SafeWork NSW media releases surfaced in the past 24 hours, with the commencement-day settings (revised Guidelines, frozen 1.99% target rate, tighter psychological-injury test, 25% WPI threshold, 130-week cap, enforceable psychosocial code — covered in the 28 June – 8 July digests) continuing to bed in. The single distinct new signal is interstate and inform-level: WorkSafe Victoria opened its 2026-27 premium renewals on 8 July with the average rate frozen at 1.8% for a fourth straight year, a scheme-sustainability comparator that reads across to NSW's own frozen Nominal Insurer target rate.
summary: Nothing materially new on the NSW scheme side in the window. Interstate, WorkSafe Victoria began issuing 2026-27 premium renewal notices online from 8 July and confirmed the average premium stays at 1.8% for a fourth consecutive year, paired with a $5.8m budget package for return-to-work support including pilots for high-risk public-sector workers. No other jurisdiction produced a materially significant, non-duplicative item.

items.headline: WorkSafe Victoria opens 2026-27 premium renewals with the average rate frozen at 1.8% for a fourth year and new return-to-work funding
items.summary: From 8 July 2026 Victorian employers can access their 2026-27 premium renewal notices through WorkSafe's Online Employer Services, with the average premium held at 1.8% of rateable remuneration — unchanged for the fourth year running. The freeze was announced alongside a $5.8m Victorian Budget 2026-27 investment in free training and tailored return-to-work support, including pilots targeting high-risk public-sector cohorts such as nurses, teachers and police.
items.so_what: Another year of a held Victorian premium sets a sustainability comparator against NSW's frozen Nominal Insurer target rate, sharpening the question of how long capped headline rates can absorb rising psychological-claim costs before scheme funding pressure forces a correction — a template NSW stakeholders will cite when the icare freeze is next tested.
